hooks.text: Scientists once feared the Moon was covered in bottomless, killer quicksand.
Why did NASA fear their first lunar lander would simply vanish?
The Moon's surface isn't solid rock; it is an electrifying, levitating fountain.

title: The Myth of the Bottomless Lunar Quicksand
description: Early scientists feared the Moon would swallow the first astronauts, but the real surface turned out to be an electrifying dust fountain.

beats.text: Scientists once feared the Moon was covered in bottomless, killer quicksand.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a lunar lander sinking into deep dust

beats.text: In the 1960s, Cornell astronomer Thomas Gold warned that lunar dust was deep enough to swallow any spacecraft.
beats.visual: Portrait of Cornell astronomer Thomas Gold

beats.text: To solve the mystery, NASA launched the Surveyor program to touch the surface before humans did.
beats.visual: Model of the NASA Surveyor spacecraft

beats.text: In June 1966, Surveyor 1 touched down on firm basaltic rock, proving the bottomless quicksand was a total myth.
beats.visual: First photograph taken from the lunar surface by Surveyor 1, 1966

beats.text: But when the sun set, robotic cameras caught a ghostly glow hovering over the horizon.
beats.visual: Photograph of the lunar horizon showing twilight glow, Surveyor 7, 1968

beats.text: Solar radiation strips electrons from the soil, creating electrostatic charges that launch dust kilometers into the sky.
beats.visual: Artist concept of electrostatic dust levitation on the Moon

beats.text: Apollo 17 astronauts even sketched these towering rays of levitating glass shards during their final mission.
beats.visual: Sketch of lunar twilight rays drawn by Apollo 17 astronauts, 1972

beats.text: This electrifying fountain proves the Moon isn't actually covered in bottomless, killer quicksand.
beats.visual: Photograph of lunar surface soil and rock, Apollo 17, 1972

better_than_last: Prioritized the bizarre electrostatic fountain twist over a standard Apollo retelling to ensure a higher payoff score.
